text: There were two obvious choices. The first was Sicily, at the toe of Italy, less than a hundred miles from Tunisia. Taking it would open the Mediterranean to Allied shipping, and offer a stepping stone into Italy itself. The second was Greece and the Balkans, where an invasion could threaten the oil, copper, chrome and bauxite that fed Germany's war industry.
